text: Globalization has changed the way people live, work, and think about their own culture. Thanks to the internet, transport, and international trade, the world has become more interconnected than ever before. As a result, ideas, products, and traditions can spread from one country to another within days. Although globalization has many benefits, it also raises questions about cultural identity. Some experts worry that global brands and media could eventually homogenize local cultures, meaning that unique traditions and customs slowly disappear. Others argue that people can embrace new global trends while still preserving their heritage. For example, a person might enjoy international films and music while also celebrating traditional festivals with their family. Migration has also played an important role in creating diverse, multicultural societies. When people move to a new country, they often need to adapt to a different language and lifestyle. However, this does not always mean that they must fully assimilate; many immigrants successfully maintain their own customs while adopting new ones, allowing different cultures to coexist. This exposure to other ways of life can give people a wider perspective, helping them understand that no single culture should be dominant over another.
